note: Sources whose own terms forbid commercial or machine use. Their rows stay on disk and are NOT read by the candidate compiler: parked, counted in miner_candidates.json intake.terms_fenced, never deleted. `match` is fnmatch patterns on the path relative to an intelligence root, forward slashes. TO REOPEN ONE: read the source's terms page, and only if it permits commercial use set `open` to true AND paste the permitting sentence into `permit_clause` with the date in `permit_read`. `open` without a clause stays closed. A fence removed from this file is still enforced if it is one of the built-in ones in terms_fences.py. `seats` names source directories and miners fenced as a whole: the miner does not fetch, and seat-based readers skip the directory. Readers call terms_fences.path_fenced / seat_fenced; nobody keeps a private copy of the rule.

fences.reason: BIS terms allow noncommercial use only
fences.clause: Use of the content is allowed for noncommercial purposes
fences.missed_growth: central bank speech titles and tone from BIS are not compiled into candidates; the same speeches are read from the banks' own sites where their terms permit (cb_own_site_speeches), so the loss is the banks not yet covered there
